about: An underground-empire adventure in the Zork tradition. You are in a final test set by an old silver-haired man. You explore a cave system with a lake, a shadowy land, a cliff and a secret stair. You are meant to prove yourself worthy before going down to him.

done.why: I saw nearly every reachable place. What was left was a dark passage south of the lake, which I could only reach without a light, and a shiny object on the lake bottom that I couldn't grab. The secret stairway told me I was not yet worthy. I had died twice and ran out of ideas.

ending.what: The old man's stairway turned me back as not yet worthy. I never found what would make me worthy.

moments.note: I tied the chest to the rope for the smiling man. He took it and left, and the rope was gone. I was stranded and he had tricked me.
Giving bread to the sleeping old man made him vanish and reveal a secret door.
The door opened onto stairs, but I was told the way down was not mine today. I had no clue what would change that.
Entering the lake made me drop everything, including the torch I had just taken. It went out for good.

A hooded figure with a sword like mine appeared, and my sword came to my hand glowing. It lowered its sword and bowed its head partway through the fight, but I killed it anyway. I may have missed a way to spare it.
The shiny object on the lake bottom kept slipping away. I drowned trying to take it.
The only way to the dark passage south of the lake was to swim there, which means no light. A grue killed me.

wished: Spare the hooded figure instead of killing it, or take its hood.
Carry a light across the lake to the south passage.
Catch the shiny thing in the lake.
Know what would make me worthy of the stairs.

lines.line: Perhaps what you seek is through there!
lines.why: The reward for the bread, and a good reveal.

lines.line: the door is open, but the way down is not yours today.
lines.why: It gives a gentle refusal and a sense of purpose.

lines.line: The water has the look of a cold that would open your hands for you, and would not give back what fell out of them
lines.why: Strong prose that hints at the lake rule.

lines.line: It lowers its sword, and its head with it, and waits; the hood hangs within reach of your hand.
lines.why: It offers a moral choice that I missed.

fun.why: The early exploring and the bread puzzle were fun. The lake rules and two deaths wore it down.

engagement.why: I was curious about the stairs and the hooded figure, but I got stuck with nothing obvious to try.

difficulty.why: Several things were hard to work out or reach: the worthiness condition, light across the lake, and the shiny object.

interestingness.why: It has a coherent premise with tests, a double, a trickster and a hidden door.

prose.why: Several lines are atmospheric and literary, especially the lake and the stair refusal.
